title: Polynomial sections and the graded ideal-power presentation on an algebraic stack
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $P$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $p:\mathcal X\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism from an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal B$ be any quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebra [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and put $B=\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B)$. Use small indexing sets in [def-weil-size-convention] and polynomial rings in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].
For every small set $L$, there is a quasi-coherent polynomial algebra $\mathcal B[x_l:l\in L]$, whose pullback to every smooth affine scheme chart $U\to\mathcal X$ is the ordinary polynomial algebra over the quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal B_U$. The coefficientwise map
$$B[x_l:l\in L]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal B[x_l:l\in L])$$
is a natural algebra isomorphism, and a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras induces a surjection of their polynomial algebras.
For an arbitrary ideal $I\subseteq P$ generated by a family $(a_j)_{j\in J}$ with $J$ small, let $\mathcal J=I\mathcal B$ be the ideal generated by the structural images of the $a_j$. The ideal powers $\mathcal J^0=\mathcal B$, $\mathcal J^{m+1}=\mathcal J\mathcal J^m$ and the algebra quotient $\mathcal B/\mathcal J$ are quasi-coherent. There is a graded quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebra
$$\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\mathcal J^m T^m$$
whose pullback to each smooth affine chart is the ordinary Rees algebra of the extended ideal in $\mathcal B_U$. There is a surjection of graded quasi-coherent algebras
$$q:\mathcal B[x_j:j\in J]\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R,\qquad x_j\longmapsto a_jT,$$
with degree-zero map the identity of $\mathcal B$ and every $x_j$ of degree one. Global sections identify, as graded algebras,
$$\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal R)=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal J^m)T^m\subseteq B[T].$$
In these identifications $\Gamma(q)$ sends $\sum_\alpha b_\alpha x^\alpha$ to $\sum_\alpha b_\alpha a^\alpha T^{|\alpha|}$. Submodule inclusions and these coefficient descriptions are asserted on smooth charts and on global sections; no preservation of ideal inclusions on arbitrary nonflat test maps is asserted. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed, and no separation of the absolute diagonal is assumed.

proof.text: Write $M_L$ for the small set of finitely supported functions $L\to\mathbf N$. Form $\mathcal P_L=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in M_L}\mathcal B e_\alpha$ by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-direct-sums]. Define multiplication by $(b e_\alpha)(c e_\beta)=bc e_{\alpha+\beta}$ and unit $1e_0$, with the structural map $b\mapsto be_0$. More explicitly, on each pair of summands use the multiplication $\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$ followed by the $(\alpha+\beta)$-summand map; the bilinear universal properties of tensor and coproducts give a map on the whole sum. Tensor products remain quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness]. The scheme-test comparison [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] and the coproduct comparison identify this multiplication with finite convolution on every smooth scheme chart, hence with the polynomial algebra of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The associative, commutative and unit identities hold there and therefore globally, since a smooth atlas detects equality of module maps by the faithful restriction in [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness]. This constructs $\mathcal B[x_l:l\in L]$, with every generator specified and no choice of a presentation.

proof.text: The quasi-compactness hypothesis on $p$ implies that $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact: in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] take the quasi-compact test $\operatorname{Spec}P$ with its identity map, so the resulting fibre product is $\mathcal X$. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-direct-sums] to the family constantly $\mathcal B$ indexed by $M_L$. It gives $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal P_L)=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in M_L}B e_\alpha$. On summands the multiplication from step 1 sends $(b,c)$ to $bc$ in summand $\alpha+\beta$, exactly the polynomial multiplication of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Thus the coefficientwise comparison is an algebra isomorphism. Every coefficient homomorphism commutes with these summand maps and products, proving naturality.

proof.text: For a surjection $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B'$, apply it to each coefficient of $\mathcal P_L$. This gives the polynomial algebra map by the multiplication formula in step 1. A section of a sheaf direct sum is locally a finite sum of coefficient sections. Each of these finitely many target coefficients lifts after an fppf cover, by the definition of surjection in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]; successively refining these finitely many covers lifts all coefficients on one covering family. Their polynomial with the same monomials lifts the given section. Consequently the polynomial map is locally surjective, as required. This is sheaf surjectivity; it does not claim surjectivity on global sections.

proof.text: Work with images in $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)$, which is abelian by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-abelian]. Define $e_1:\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$ by $(b_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_jb_j$ and set $\mathcal J=\operatorname{im}(e_1)$, with its image monomorphism to $\mathcal B$. The source is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-direct-sums]. Smooth restriction preserves this image by exactness [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-qcoh-exact], so on every smooth affine chart it is precisely the ordinary extended ideal generated by the $a_j$. The image is a $\mathcal B$-ideal: multiplication by $b$ preserves the kernel of $e_1$ since $e_1(bv)=b e_1(v)$, so the action descends to its image; equivalently this factorization can be checked on smooth charts using faithful restriction [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness]. Its cokernel $\mathcal B/\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent and is the module-sheaf cokernel by that same node. The ideal property makes this cokernel an algebra quotient. This specifies exactly the smooth-chart ideal convention in the statement; an image monomorphism in quasi-coherent modules need not be injective on nonflat big-site tests.

proof.text: For $m\geq0$ let $M_{J,m}=\{\alpha:J\to\mathbf N\text{ finitely supported}:|\alpha|=m\}$ and let $e_m:\bigoplus_{\alpha\in M_{J,m}}\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$ have coefficient maps multiplication by $a^\alpha$. Take its image $K_m$ in the same abelian category. For $m=0$, $e_0$ is the identity and $K_0=\mathcal B$; for $m=1$ it gives $\mathcal J$. Smooth exact restriction identifies $K_m$ with the ideal generated by the products $a^\alpha$ of total degree $m$. Inductively these are the ordinary powers: multiplying a degree-$m$ product by a generator gives a degree-$(m+1)$ product, and every degree-$(m+1)$ product has such a factorization, by choosing an index with positive exponent. Finite sums of these products give both inclusions. Tensor products and images are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness, lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-abelian]; the same exact smooth restriction therefore identifies the image of $\mathcal J\otimes K_m\to\mathcal B$ with $K_{m+1}$. Faithful atlas restriction detects this equality of subobjects. Thus $K_m=\mathcal J^m$ and all stated powers are quasi-coherent. Products $K_m\otimes K_n\to K_{m+n}$ are induced by multiplying generator products, since $a^\alpha a^\beta=a^{\alpha+\beta}$; they agree with ordinary ideal multiplication on smooth charts.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}K_mT^m$ using [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-direct-sums]. The product maps of step 5 give graded multiplication; the unit is $1\in K_0=\mathcal B$. Associativity and commutativity follow from those in $\mathcal B$ on every smooth chart, hence globally by faithful atlas restriction [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness]. By the coproduct comparison and step 5 its smooth affine restriction is $\bigoplus_m(\mathcal J_U)^mT^m$, with coefficientwise inclusion into $\mathcal B_U[T]$; this is the ordinary Rees algebra of [def-nagata-rees-algebra]. The elements $a_j\in K_1$ come from the $j$-summand maps defining $e_1$. Define $q$ on the $\alpha$-summand of $\mathcal P_J$ by multiplication by $a^\alpha$, corestricted to $K_{|\alpha|}T^{|\alpha|}$ through $e_{|\alpha|}$. The identity $a^\alpha a^\beta=a^{\alpha+\beta}$ makes it an algebra map. Its degree-zero part is the identity, and $q(x_j)=a_jT$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.1, printed p.507; Lemma 4.1.8, printed p.503. Published PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED. Explicit module construction and degree-zero completion supplied by the worker.

proof.text: In degree $m$ the map $q$ is exactly the factorization of $e_m$ onto its image $K_m$. This is an epimorphism in quasi-coherent modules. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness] it is locally surjective as a map of fppf module sheaves. Any local section of $\mathcal R$, being a section of the sheaf coproduct of the $K_m$, locally uses finitely many degrees. Refine the lifting covers for those finitely many coefficient sections, and add their lifts in the corresponding degree pieces of $\mathcal P_J$. This lifts the section through $q$. Hence $q$ is a surjection of graded quasi-coherent algebras.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.1, printed p.507; Lemma 4.1.8, printed p.503. Published PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED. Explicit module construction and degree-zero completion supplied by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-direct-sums] to $(K_m)_{m\geq0}$. This yields $\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal R)=\bigoplus_m\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal J^m)T^m$ as modules and, by the products in step 6, as graded algebras. Each image monomorphism $K_m\to\mathcal B$ induces an injection on global sections: a section is the same as an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-linear map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to K_m$ (send $1$ to the section), so injectivity is precisely cancellation of a monomorphism in the full category of quasi-coherent modules. The compatible-family definition is [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Applying these injections coefficientwise embeds the displayed algebra in $B[T]$, with finite support guaranteed by the direct-sum comparison. On the $\alpha$-summand the definition of $q$ is multiplication by $a^\alpha$ in degree $|\alpha|$. Combining this with step 2 gives $\Gamma(q)(\sum_\alpha b_\alpha x^\alpha)=\sum_\alpha b_\alpha a^\alpha T^{|\alpha|}$. All sums and products used here have finite support per section; no finite generating set, exactness of global sections, or separation of the absolute diagonal entered.

(8) Γ = Hom(O,-) and cancelling the QCoh monomorphism gives the injection into B[T]. Small cases checked: L empty, J empty, I=(1), nilpotent I, X empty, and a non-quasi-compact counterexample.
